title: After a firewall cleanup, nobody can SSH into anything
intro: A security review deleted all firewall rules allowing port 22 'from anywhere'. Since then, 'gcloud compute ssh --tunnel-through-iap' fails for every VM with 'failed to connect to backend'. The on-call engineer needs to get onto db-1 (europe-west1-b) right now.

steps.prompt: Diagnose SSH to db-1 (europe-west1-b) through IAP.
steps.fake_output:
---- Checking network connectivity ----
No ingress firewall rule allows traffic from the IAP range 35.235.240.0/20 to port 22 on db-1.
---- Checking user permissions ----
User has roles/iap.tunnelResourceAccessor. OK.

steps.prompt: List the remaining ingress rules on prod-vpc that allow port 22.
expected_commands: gcloud compute firewall-rules list --filter="network=prod-vpc AND allowed[].ports:22"
gcloud compute firewall-rules list --filter='network=prod-vpc AND allowed[].ports:22'
steps.hint: Filter on network and allowed ports.

steps.prompt: The cleanup also deleted the IAP rule (source 35.235.240.0/20), because it 'looked like' an SSH rule. Recreate it on prod-vpc as allow-iap-ssh, TCP 22 from 35.235.240.0/20 only.
expected_commands: gcloud compute firewall-rules create allow-iap-ssh --network prod-vpc --direction INGRESS --allow tcp:22 --source-ranges 35.235.240.0/20
gcloud compute firewall-rules create allow-iap-ssh --network prod-vpc --allow tcp:22 --source-ranges 35.235.240.0/20
steps.fake_output:
Creating firewall...done.
NAME           NETWORK   DIRECTION  PRIORITY  ALLOW   DENY  DISABLED
allow-iap-ssh  prod-vpc  INGRESS    1000      tcp:22        False

resolution: The security review had the right goal: port 22 open to 0.0.0.0/0 is an invitation to brute-force attacks. But it deleted every port-22 rule by pattern, including the one rule that made SSH safe: allowing only Google's IAP range 35.235.240.0/20. With IAP, the VM never accepts SSH from the internet; Google's proxy authenticates each user with IAM and then connects from that range. Without the rule, even correctly authorised users can't reach anything. Lessons: firewall cleanups should classify rules by source range, not by port, since 0.0.0.0/0 is the danger and 35.235.240.0/20 is the fix; give the IAP rule a name and description that say why it must stay; and keep a break-glass path, such as the serial console (with its own IAM control), that doesn't depend on the firewall at all.
